title: System scalar mates equal projection maps with refinement normalization
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings $R\subset S$, uniformizers $\pi,v$, and ramification index $e$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For $n\ge1$ put $A_n=R/\pi^n$ and $B_n=S/\pi^nS=S/v^{en}$, with the actual quotient transitions. Fix one $R$-basis of $S$ and use its reductions at every level [lem-coef-finite-free-extension]. On fixed small pro-etale sites of separated finite-type $k$-schemes $W$, let $\mathscr S_{A,W}$ and $\mathscr S_{B,W}$ be the abelian categories of strict semilinear module systems: objects are module sheaves $M_n$ with linear maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}M_n$, and morphisms are componentwise maps commuting with these transitions [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Use their ordinary unbounded derived categories. Let $U_W$ be termwise restriction from $B_\bullet$ to $A_\bullet$ and $T_W=-\otimes^L_{A_\bullet}B_\bullet$ derived scalar extension [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

Let $h:V\to W$ be separated of finite type and fix a compactification $c=(V\xrightarrow{j}\overline V\xrightarrow{p}W)$, with $j$ open and $p$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Put $\mathcal F^c_{h,C}=Rp_{*,C}j_{!,C}$ on simultaneous derived coefficient systems [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization]. Use the canonical restriction/geometry comparisons and scalar adjunction of [lem-coef-finite-free-system-restriction]. Let $M\in D(\mathscr S_{A,V})$ be normalized, with each $M_n$ bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude; no common cohomological or Tor interval in $n$ is required [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Define $a_p:T_WRp_{*,A}\to Rp_{*,B}T_{\overline V}$ to be the $p_B^*\dashv Rp_{*,B}$ transpose of $T_{\overline V}(\varepsilon_{p,A})$ after $p_B^*T_W\cong T_{\overline V}p_A^*$. Let $b_j:T_{\overline V}j_{!,A}\cong j_{!,B}T_V$ be the canonical open tensor balancing map [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate, lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Put
$$c^c_{h,M}=Rp_{*,B}(b_{j,M})\,a_{p,j_{!,A}M}:T_W\mathcal F^c_{h,A}M\longrightarrow\mathcal F^c_{h,B}T_VM.$$

Under $U_WT_WP\cong P\otimes^L_{A_\bullet}B_{\bullet,W}$ and $U\mathcal F^c_{h,B}\cong\mathcal F^c_{h,A}U$, there is an equality of specified maps
$$U_W(c^c_{h,M})=\operatorname{PF}^{c,\mathrm{sys}}_{h,M,B_\bullet}.$$
Here the right side is the strict-system projection map: the $p_A^*\dashv Rp_{*,A}$ transpose of $(\varepsilon_{p,A}\otimes1)\mu_p$, followed by the open tensor comparison, where $\mu_p$ is the canonical pullback/tensor identification [def-exchange-projection, lem-pur-system-level-projection-formula-coherence]. The equality holds in $D(\mathscr S_{A,W})$ before evaluation. The map $c^c_{h,M}$ is also the scalar-adjunction mate of $\mathcal F^c_{h,A}U\cong U\mathcal F^c_{h,B}$; its level-$n$ evaluation is the finite proper-counit/open-balancing coefficient comparison. It is an isomorphism, and in the fixed reduced basis its restriction is finite-sum distributivity [lem-pur-finite-free-compact-composition].

For any proper refinement $u:c'\to c$, let $\theta_{u,C}:\mathcal F^{c'}_{h,C}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F^c_{h,C}$ be the canonical system refinement comparisons [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism, lem-pur-system-compactification-pf-substitution]. Then
$$\theta_{u,B,T_VM}\,c^{c'}_{h,M}=c^c_{h,M}\,T_W(\theta_{u,A,M})$$
as maps of derived $B_\bullet$-systems before evaluation or inverse limit. These squares respect identity and composable refinements. Comparisons through a common refinement are independent of the common refinement and satisfy the cocycle for three compactifications. The maps and equations use the actual quotient transitions and the same fixed reduced basis; no conclusion is inferred merely from levelwise equality.

proof.text: Use the unchanged scalar projection data [def-coef-system-scalar-projection-data]. Obtain the normalized system tensor and finite-level constituents from [lem-coef-system-scalar-tensor-constituents]. Obtain the simultaneous reduced basis and its summand equations from [lem-coef-system-scalar-basis-distributivity]. The tensor constituent assertion deliberately omits scalar-comparison invertibility and all refinement equations.

For the compact support functor F and its scalar comparison q after restriction, write i_a and p_a for the source basis coordinates, and j_a and r_a for the target coordinates. The summand equation is j_a q=F(i_a). Define t=sum_a F(p_a) j_a. Then t q=F(sum_a p_a i_a)=1. Inserting sum_a r_a j_a=1 before q and using i_a p_b=delta_ab proves q t=1. The compact-support restriction comparison is invertible, so restricted scalar comparison is invertible. Ordinary restriction reflects isomorphisms because it leaves underlying abelian sheaves unchanged; exact derived restriction reflects them by the homology criterion. Thus every scalar comparison is invertible. Assemble Identification with the normalized constituent equations.

Obtain lower refinement coherence, lower and upper gamma invertibility, the restriction theta square, and lower theta naturality at the scalar unit from [lem-coef-system-scalar-refinement-restriction]. Apply the injective scalar-adjunction Hom equivalence to the desired B-linear refinement square. Rewrite its two sides by the scalar-mate equations. Move the inverse restriction comparison through restricted theta using the restriction square. Lower theta naturality at the scalar unit identifies the resulting expressions. This proves the square in the upper system category without assuming restriction faithful on morphisms.

Gamma invertibility makes each lower and upper theta invertible. For a common span (a,b), use the refinement square for a and b, precompose by T(theta_a), and cancel theta_a and theta_a,B inverses to get c_1 Theta_B=T(Theta_A)c_2. For identity and composition precompose the desired upper equation by the invertible scalar comparison, rewrite the refinement square and lower law, and cancel. For common-span independence and cocycle do the same with the span square. Functoriality and cancellation prove the upper laws from the lower laws.
